extracted.intended_audience: researchers, clinicians, and methodologists who develop, validate, or audit clinical/observational measurement instruments and assess inter-rater reliability
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and empirical criteria used in studies to design, execute, and interpret inter-rater and intra-rater reliability, validity, feasibility, and measurement-error assessments for clinical, observational, imaging, and web-based instruments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of inter-rater reliability indices
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess agreement using statistics such as Cohen's kappa, weighted kappa, Fleiss' kappa, intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC), and percent agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the agreement metric appropriate to the data type (categorical vs continuous) and study design; report multiple indices where informative (e.g., kappa for categorical epochs, ICC for continuous scores).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation thresholds for kappa
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard test-retest criteria consider Kappa values: 0.0 to 0.40 poor to fair, 0.41 to 0.60 moderate, 0.61 to 0.80 substantial, and 0.81 to 1.00 as almost perfect reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these ranges to contextualize kappa values when reporting reliability; note that interpretation can vary and be affected by prevalence and bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intra-rater (test-retest) reliability procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate intra-rater reliability using test-retest designs with a specified time interval between readings (e.g., ~4 hours, 2-week intervals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify and justify retest interval; report kappa/ICC for repeat readings and consider effects of memory or true change over the interval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feasibility metrics for scoring instruments
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure feasibility via clinician-reported clarity and time-to-complete (example: 95% of respondents reported the ICU Mobility Scale took <1 min to complete).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report user burden (time) and perceived clarity/acceptability alongside reliability results to judge practicality in clinical settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validity types and procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess criterion validity, construct validity, and concurrent validity by comparing instrument scores to clinical evaluations, established instruments, or objective measures (e.g., correlation of K&L grading with MOAKS, correlation of observational MVPA with accelerometry).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report appropriate statistics (Spearman/Pearson correlations, sensitivity/specificity, LR+, LR-) and blind raters to comparison data when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsiveness as a clinimetric property
rubrics_metrics.description: Include responsiveness (ability to detect change) among evaluated clinimetric properties; note that some studies plan to assess responsiveness in larger follow-up populations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan longitudinal or pre/post designs to assess sensitivity to clinically meaningful change and report responsiveness indices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear operational definitions and screening criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Reliability improves when screening criteria or item definitions are clearly defined (example: detection of 41 screening criteria in medical record review required clearly defining SC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop unambiguous item definitions and decision rules prior to rater training and testing to reduce disagreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer training and standardization
rubrics_metrics.description: Well-organized training programs for reviewers are required to get more reliable results (noted for hospital adverse event studies and CME peer-review audits).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide standardized training, practice cases, and calibration exercises; educate raters on domain-specific and procedure-specific requirements (e.g., CME validation specifics).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of standardized scoring forms and blinding
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ standardized scoring forms and blind raters to clinical information, radiology reports, and other rater results to reduce bias (used in MRI-based grading studies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide explicit scoring forms and ensure blinding where feasible; report blinding procedures in methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for prevalence effects and low-frequency categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Be aware that low prevalence of positive scorings in some subcategories can produce wide variability in kappa (examples: MRI classification subcategories with low positive prevalence showed κ range -0.05 to 1.00).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report prevalence, consider alternative indices, and interpret kappa in context of item prevalence and marginal distributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample and rater composition considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Design studies with an adequate number and mix of raters and participants (examples: multiple therapists and nursing staff, 100 consecutive patients, or enriched samples for specific findings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select representative samples and rater panels that reflect intended clinical use; report rater experience level and sampling/enrichment strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combine agreement measures for different data types
rubrics_metrics.description: For binary variables report percent agreement and Cohen's kappa; for continuous measures report ICC and Bland-Altman plots with Limits of Agreement (LoA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use complementary statistics to fully describe agreement and measurement error; present LoA relative to clinical measurement ranges to judge acceptability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instrument updating and iterative revision
rubrics_metrics.description: Instruments/checklists should be updated as the environment changes (example: SNACZ food store checklist should be updated as a wider variety of healthier alternatives become available).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan periodic reviews and revisions of item content to maintain instrument relevance and validity over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit defect/category taxonomies for audit tasks
rubrics_metrics.description: When auditing durable materials (e.g., CME slides), construct explicit categories of defects such as: (1) insufficient citation, (2) poor formatting, (3) nonacknowledgment of non‑FDA‑approved use, (4) misapplied data, (5) 1‑sided data, (6) self‑ or institutional promotion, (7) conflict of interest/commercial bias, (8) other, (9) no defect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use prespecified defect categories to structure peer-review audits; however, expect subjectivity and provide rater training on category definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for high consistency for real-time central review
rubrics_metrics.description: Real-time central review processes that determine treatment assignment (e.g., surgical reviews for trial stratification) require very high inter-rater reliability across assessed variables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Validate central review procedures empirically; report kappa/ICC values per variable and accept only variables with proven high agreement for decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation for further training and test standardization when reliability is variable
rubrics_metrics.description: When some clinical tests show poor reliability, additional training and further test standardization are recommended to improve reliability (noted for spinal screening tests).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify low-reliability items and iteratively refine test protocols and rater instruction to raise agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare measurement error to assessment range
rubrics_metrics.description: Limits of Agreement (LoA) should be evaluated relative to the range of assessments to determine whether measurement error is acceptable (example: wide LoA compared with assessment range calls reliability into question).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present LoA alongside the clinical or operational range of the measure to inform acceptability for screening or diagnostic use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two‑axis annotation scheme for web health documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Annotate consumer medical web pages along two axes: (1) reliability (extent to which medical information can be trusted) and (2) page type (patient leaflet, commercial, link, medical article, testimonial, or support).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop and pilot classification rubrics for each axis; measure inter-rater agreement (accuracy, F-measure, kappa) and refine classes that show poor agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of content validity and clinical utility
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure content validity and clinical utility (examples: SAAIA showed good to high percent agreement for content validity and fair agreement for clinical utility).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use expert panels and target users to rate content validity and utility; report percent agreement and kappa where applicable and refine items with poor utility ratings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observational sampling and timing procedures for activity measures
rubrics_metrics.description: For observational systems (e.g., OSRAC:YS) use momentary time-sampling procedures (e.g., 10-second observe, 20-second record) and calculate kappa for categorical context codes and ICC for percent time estimates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standardize observation intervals and coder protocols; validate observational estimates against objective measures (accelerometry) for concurrent validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of sensitivity, specificity, and likelihood ratios in instrument validation
rubrics_metrics.description: Report diagnostic accuracy metrics such as sensitivity, specificity, positive and negative likelihood ratios when validating instruments against clinical assessments or records (example: Q-DFD comparisons yielded sensitivity, specificity, LR+, LR-).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide confidence intervals and interpret accuracy metrics in context of intended use (screening vs diagnostic).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate anatomical or subcategory reliability separately
rubrics_metrics.description: For multi-part classification systems (e.g., MRI grading/classification), assess reliability for overall categories and for anatomical subcategories separately because subcategory reliability may differ markedly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report κ/ICC per subcategory; highlight subcategories with low prevalence or unclear reliability and consider collapsing or redefining them.
